dedupe_keys.name: mining gym configurable rl benchmarking environment for open pit truck dispatch

description: An open-source discrete-event simulator of open-pit mine haulage for testing dispatch methods. The arXiv paper 2503.19195 by Banerjee and co-authors at Queensland University of Technology says Mining-Gym is built on Salabim discrete-event simulation and integrates with Gymnasium so that reinforcement learning algorithms from Stable Baselines3 can be trained, and that it captures mining uncertainties such as equipment failures and queue congestion, with a graphical interface, logging and visualisation. The paper compares heuristics with learned scheduling across six scenarios, from normal operation to severe equipment failures. The code is free to download from GitHub under the MIT licence. Coverage is configurable mine scenarios, not a real site. Caveats: scenarios are synthetic and the page read gives no validation against mine records. For simulation it tests how haulage output falls and recovers when trucks or shovels break down. A related catalogue record is the OpenMines truck dispatching simulator.
